newsitem.title: PERU: Peru mediators urge rebel leader to start talks.
newsitem.headline: Peru mediators urge rebel leader to start talks.

text.p: Mediators in Peru's hostage crisis held a "cordial" meeting on Thursday with the leader of Marxist rebels holding 72 VIPs at the Japanese ambassador's home to persuade him to resume talks to end the 51-day siege.

"I hope that with the participation of everyone we will find that light of a peaceful solution," Roman Catholic Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani told reporters outside the residence, where he spent 2-1/2 hours along with Red Cross representative Michel Minnig and Canadian Ambassador Anthony Vincent.

They are part of a four-member panel of "guarantors" for eventual talks between rebel leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini and chief government negotiator Domingo Palermo, who have not held face-to-face talks since Dec. 28. The fourth, Japanese representative Terusuke Tarada, was not present on Thursday.

Cipriani said the 72 hostages, held by about 15 well-armed Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas since Dec. 17, were bearing up well. "We found the situation of the hostages favourable, quiet, obviously tired by the prolonged time" of their captivity, he said.

Peru's President Alberto Fujimori, whose younger brother is among the captives, promised Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto last weekend that he would resume direct talks with the MRTA. But he insists he will not give in to the rebels' demand that about 400 jailed comrades be freed.
The guerrillas sang their now-daily songs on Thursday morning and vowed to resist until their demands were met.

Fujimori said on Wednesday his government was organising meetings on "logistics" to start formal talks with Cerpa. "We then hope to define the sequence of these preliminary conversations (with the MRTA)," he told reporters.
Government officials say they have selected a building near the residence to hold the talks and a bullet-proof vehicle has been arranged to take Cerpa to the site.
Although he has flatly rejected the main rebel demand, Fujimori has raised the possibility of easing harsh prison conditions and allowing the rebels to seek asylum abroad.

Outside the residence on Thursday, several dozen women from a local women's centre organised a peaceful sit-down protest. They arranged white flowers in a circle on the floor and set out banners in four languanges urging the two sides to start talks to end the crisis.

The MRTA has released most of the nearly VIP captives it seized when it stormed a garden party at the residence seven weeks ago. But it has held on to its most valuable hostages, including two government ministers, the Japanese and Bolivian ambassadors and Japanese diplomats and businessmen.
